All 7 review issues hold up against the code: 2 need a code change and 5 are optional cleanups (one of those duplicates another). No code was changed and nothing was posted. I wrote the verdicts to `verdicts.json` and confirmed it parses as JSON.

| # | Category | Verdict | Actionable | Key evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | NITPICK | VALID | OPTIONAL | Typo "Succesful" in a comment at `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:413`. |
| 1 | BEST-PRACTICE | VALID | OPTIONAL | At `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:290-296` and `:311-317`, `findElement` never returns null, so the null check is pointless. The broad `catch (Exception)` can hide unrelated browser-driver errors. If the element does exist, the test still fails properly, so this is about test quality, not a bug. Before this PR the codebase already used `Assert.assertThrows(NoSuchElementException.class, …)` for this check. |
| 2 | CORRECTNESS | VALID | **YES** | `UsernameForm.java:47` calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments. The only version is `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel)` at `UsernamePasswordForm.java:160`, so the code doesn't compile. The latest commit changed the method's signature but didn't update this call. |
| 3 | CORRECTNESS | VALID | **YES** | The `user != null` check at `UsernamePasswordForm.java:161` means the passkey login data is never set up on the first login page (callers at `:115` and `:137`). That's a regression: before the PR, it was set up exactly when there was no user. It also contradicts the PR's own tests, which expect the passkey form on the first login page. |
| 4 | CONVENTION | VALID | OPTIONAL | `PasswordCredentialModel` is imported at `PasskeysUsernamePasswordFormTest.java:35` and never used. It doesn't break the build, and I found no style-check rule against unused imports. |
| 5 | BEST-PRACTICE | VALID | OPTIONAL | Same point as #1. |
| 6 | NITPICK | VALID | OPTIONAL | `WebAuthnConditionalUIAuthenticator.java:65` overrides the method at `WebAuthnAuthenticator.java:128` without `@Override`. |

**Fix first:** #2 and #3 are the same problem. The fix is to drop the `user != null` check and have `UsernameForm` pass `context.getUser()`. Until then the PR doesn't compile and passkey login on the first login page is broken.
